Definition: neuter of a derivative of G5442; a guard-case, i.e. "phylactery" for wearing slips of Scripture texts:-- phylactery.
BiblicalUsage: A phylakterion was a little case worn on the forehead or arm holding slips of Scripture. Jesus names it once, in Matthew 23:5, when He says the Pharisees make broad their phylacteries, and enlarge the borders of their garments — the word itself became a picture of religion worn for show.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that Scripture carried on the outside and ignored on the inside is the oldest form of hypocrisy.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
